When a name qualifies, it is listed here first — with ticker, price, P/E, forward P/E, RSI, sector, weeks touching, FCF yield, revenue growth, volume ratio and insider activity — and also flagged in the tables below. Use the 🔶 filter above the tables to isolate them.
Flags 💎 Undervalued — trailing P/E < 12 & forward P/E < 15, no high-debt flag 🔻 Oversold — 14-week RSI < 30 Screaming buy — undervalued and oversold (see section above) 🔶 Near screaming buy — applies on both tabs (Weekly uses 14-week RSI, Monthly uses 14-month RSI): one leg in full, close on the other, no high debt — undervalued with RSI 30–40, or oversold with P/E 12–20 & fwd P/E < 15 (Weekly: 10 names today — C (Citigroup Inc.), CFG (Citizens Financial Group, Inc.), CMI (Cummins Inc.), COF (Capital One Financial Corporation) and 6 more · Monthly: 1 name on the Nov intra-month list — ALNY (Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc.)) ⚠️ High debt — D/E > 2× or net debt > 50% of market cap 🔥 SQUEEZE = possible short squeeze setup: ≥10% of float short and ≥3 days to cover 📈 4H SMA ↑ / ➡️ 4H SMA → — 20-period SMA on 4-hour bars: ↑ rose more than 0.5% over the last 5 bars (~3 trading days), → flat within ±0.5%; no pill when it is falling 🪤 Potential trap: at least 3 of 5 warning signs — missed earnings last quarter; earnings expected to fall sharply (forward P/E over 1.5× trailing); negative cash flow or profitability; debt stress (interest cover under 1.5×, or high debt with cover under 2.5×); insiders or big funds selling heavily. Hover the pill for the reasons on that stock. 💸 Burning Cash — interest cover below 1.5× and cash runway under 2 years (cash ÷ annual cash burn). Earnings barely cover the interest bill and the cash pile runs out within two years at the current burn rate. 🎯 Potential opportunity: at least 4 of 5 positive signs — beat earnings in 2 of the last 3 quarters; net cash with comfortable interest cover; strong growth and cash generation (Rule of 40 over 40, positive cash flow); insiders or big funds buying; P/E below its 15-year median with forward P/E under 15. Hover the pill for the reasons on that stock. 💧 Diluting — shares outstanding up 10% or more over 3 years; each share owns a shrinking slice of the company. ✂️ Buyback — shares outstanding down 10% or more over 3 years; buybacks shrank the share count, so each share owns a bigger slice. Score Score = buy score out of 10: Value, Health, Timing, Backing, Sentiment (2 points each). Tiers: 9–10 Strongest, 7–8 Solid, 4–6 Mixed, 0–3 Weak. RSI = 14-bar Wilder’s RSI on closed bars, shown under the Score; the arrow is the move vs the prior bar (↑ improving, ↓ worsening, → flat); below 30 is oversold. Sentiment = analyst consensus (Buy or better) + options flow (put/call volume below 1.0 = bullish). Columns Short = % of float sold short; days to cover underneath (days of average volume shorts need to exit) R40 = Rule of 40: revenue growth % + margin %; (EBITDA) uses EBITDA margin, (FCF) uses free cash flow margin. Bold green above 40%, red when negative, with the dominant leg’s % shown on the driver line. Margin trend = latest quarter’s EBITDA margin vs a year ago, in percentage points. Growth / Margin Driven — which leg contributes more than half of the Rule of 40 score: revenue growth or EBITDA margin. Insider = net $ of open-market insider trades, last 3 months (actual traded values from filings; awards and option exercises excluded) Insider $ highlighted green when net buying > $5M, red when net selling > $25M (last 3 months) 13F = major buys/sells by 15 famous active funds, Q3 2026 (filed Nov 2026). Major = new position, full exit (both ≥ $10M), or a change over $100M or 25% of the position. Funds: Buffett, Ackman, Tiger, Coatue, Lone Pine, Viking, Third Point, Tepper, Druckenmiller, Einhorn, Klarman, Soros, Elliott, D1, Cohen (Point72 is a multi-manager fund, so its moves reflect many independent pods). vs High = price vs highest price in the last 12 months (intraday, split-adjusted) Vol = last closed week’s volume vs its 20-week average; above 1.0× means heavier than usual; highlighted yellow at 2.0× or more Cash / Debt = total cash vs total debt; green cash = cash ≥ 2× debt, red debt = debt ≥ 2× cash (C = cash, D = debt) P/S & FCF: price/sales plus trailing-12-month free cash flow; YoY = latest quarter vs same quarter last year (quarterly FCF is lumpy — a near-zero quarter a year ago can make YoY very large) Avg P/E = median annual P/E over the last 10 / 15 fiscal years (actual year count in parentheses after each value). P/E (High) = the P/E at the stock’s 12-month high price, at current earnings Yellow P/E — earnings are too small or too distorted for the P/E to mean much; P/S shown bold amber on those rows — judge on P/S instead. P/E color — the P/E value wears a pill: green when cheap (25% or more below its own 15-year median and/or its sector median), red when expensive (25% or more above), plain when in between or the two disagree. Hover the P/E to see both comparisons. Earnings: latest quarter’s EPS surprise vs the analyst consensus — green at +5% or more, red at −5% or less, plain in between — with revenue growth year-over-year underneath. Revenue growth is green at +30% or more, red at −10% or less. The dots show the last three reported quarters, latest first. Cover: interest coverage — operating earnings ÷ interest expense. Green at 3× or more (healthy); amber from 1.5× to 3× (thin cover); red below 1.5× (interest not covered from earnings; negative means an operating loss). Banks and ETFs show no figure.

Flags 💎 Undervalued — trailing P/E < 12 & forward P/E < 15, no high-debt flag 🔻 Oversold (monthly) — 14-month RSI < 30 Monthly screaming buy — undervalued and oversold on monthly RSI 🔶 Near screaming buy — applies on both tabs (Monthly uses 14-month RSI): undervalued with monthly RSI 30–40, or oversold with P/E 12–20 & fwd P/E < 15, no high debt (1 name on the Nov intra-month list — ALNY) ⚠️ High debt — D/E > 2× or net debt > 50% of market cap 🔥 SQUEEZE = possible short squeeze setup: ≥10% of float short and ≥3 days to cover 📈 4H SMA ↑ / ➡️ 4H SMA → — 20-period SMA on 4-hour bars: ↑ rose more than 0.5% over the last 5 bars (~3 trading days), → flat within ±0.5%; no pill when it is falling 🪤 Potential trap: at least 3 of 5 warning signs — missed earnings last quarter; earnings expected to fall sharply (forward P/E over 1.5× trailing); negative cash flow or profitability; debt stress (interest cover under 1.5×, or high debt with cover under 2.5×); insiders or big funds selling heavily. Hover the pill for the reasons on that stock. 💸 Burning Cash — interest cover below 1.5× and cash runway under 2 years (cash ÷ annual cash burn). Earnings barely cover the interest bill and the cash pile runs out within two years at the current burn rate. 🎯 Potential opportunity: at least 4 of 5 positive signs — beat earnings in 2 of the last 3 quarters; net cash with comfortable interest cover; strong growth and cash generation (Rule of 40 over 40, positive cash flow); insiders or big funds buying; P/E below its 15-year median with forward P/E under 15. Hover the pill for the reasons on that stock. 💧 Diluting — shares outstanding up 10% or more over 3 years; each share owns a shrinking slice of the company. ✂️ Buyback — shares outstanding down 10% or more over 3 years; buybacks shrank the share count, so each share owns a bigger slice. Score Score = buy score out of 10: Value, Health, Timing, Backing, Sentiment (2 points each). Tiers: 9–10 Strongest, 7–8 Solid, 4–6 Mixed, 0–3 Weak. RSI = 14-bar Wilder’s RSI on closed bars, shown under the Score; the arrow is the move vs the prior bar (↑ improving, ↓ worsening, → flat); below 30 is oversold. Sentiment = analyst consensus (Buy or better) + options flow (put/call volume below 1.0 = bullish). Columns Short = % of float sold short; days to cover underneath (days of average volume shorts need to exit) R40 = Rule of 40: revenue growth % + margin %; (EBITDA) uses EBITDA margin, (FCF) uses free cash flow margin. Bold green above 40%, red when negative, with the dominant leg’s % shown on the driver line. Margin trend = latest quarter’s EBITDA margin vs a year ago, in percentage points. Growth / Margin Driven — which leg contributes more than half of the Rule of 40 score: revenue growth or EBITDA margin. Insider = net $ of open-market insider trades, last 3 months (actual traded values from filings; awards and option exercises excluded) Insider $ highlighted green when net buying > $5M, red when net selling > $25M (last 3 months) 13F = major buys/sells by 15 famous active funds, Q3 2026 (filed Nov 2026). Major = new position, full exit (both ≥ $10M), or a change over $100M or 25% of the position. Funds: Buffett, Ackman, Tiger, Coatue, Lone Pine, Viking, Third Point, Tepper, Druckenmiller, Einhorn, Klarman, Soros, Elliott, D1, Cohen (Point72 is a multi-manager fund, so its moves reflect many independent pods). vs High = price vs highest price in the last 12 months (intraday, split-adjusted) Vol = last closed month’s volume vs its 20-month average; above 1.0× means heavier than usual; highlighted yellow at 2.0× or more Cash / Debt = total cash vs total debt; green cash = cash ≥ 2× debt, red debt = debt ≥ 2× cash (C = cash, D = debt) P/S & FCF: price/sales plus trailing-12-month free cash flow; YoY = latest quarter vs same quarter last year (quarterly FCF is lumpy — a near-zero quarter a year ago can make YoY very large) Avg P/E = median annual P/E over the last 10 / 15 fiscal years (actual year count in parentheses after each value). P/E (High) = the P/E at the stock’s 12-month high price, at current earnings Yellow P/E — earnings are too small or too distorted for the P/E to mean much; P/S shown bold amber on those rows — judge on P/S instead. P/E color — the P/E value wears a pill: green when cheap (25% or more below its own 15-year median and/or its sector median), red when expensive (25% or more above), plain when in between or the two disagree. Hover the P/E to see both comparisons. Earnings: latest quarter’s EPS surprise vs the analyst consensus — green at +5% or more, red at −5% or less, plain in between — with revenue growth year-over-year underneath. Revenue growth is green at +30% or more, red at −10% or less. The dots show the last three reported quarters, latest first. Cover: interest coverage — operating earnings ÷ interest expense. Green at 3× or more (healthy); amber from 1.5× to 3× (thin cover); red below 1.5× (interest not covered from earnings; negative means an operating loss). Banks and ETFs show no figure.

When a name qualifies, it is listed here first — with ticker, price, P/E, forward P/E, RSI, sector, weeks touching, FCF yield, revenue growth, volume ratio and insider activity — and also flagged in the tables below. Use the 🔶 filter above the tables to isolate them.
Flags 🔺 Overvalued — trailing P/E above its own 15y median (10y fallback) & forward P/E above 20 🔶 Near screaming sell — overvalued with RSI 60–70, or overbought with P/E above its median & fwd P/E 15–20, no high-debt condition either way (Weekly: 5 names today) Screaming sell — overvalued and overbought (see section above) 💎 Undervalued — trailing P/E < 12 & forward P/E < 15, no high-debt flag (a name can sit at the upper band and still be cheap on earnings) ⚠️ High debt — D/E > 2× or net debt > 50% of market cap 🔥 SQUEEZE = possible short squeeze setup: ≥10% of float short and ≥3 days to cover 📈 4H SMA ↑ / ➡️ 4H SMA → — 20-period SMA on 4-hour bars: ↑ rose more than 0.5% over the last 5 bars (~3 trading days), → flat within ±0.5%; no pill when it is falling 🪤 Potential trap: at least 3 of 5 warning signs — missed earnings last quarter; earnings expected to fall sharply (forward P/E over 1.5× trailing); negative cash flow or profitability; debt stress (interest cover under 1.5×, or high debt with cover under 2.5×); insiders or big funds selling heavily. Hover the pill for the reasons on that stock. 💸 Burning Cash — interest cover below 1.5× and cash runway under 2 years (cash ÷ annual cash burn). Earnings barely cover the interest bill and the cash pile runs out within two years at the current burn rate. 🎯 Potential opportunity: at least 4 of 5 positive signs — beat earnings in 2 of the last 3 quarters; net cash with comfortable interest cover; strong growth and cash generation (Rule of 40 over 40, positive cash flow); insiders or big funds buying; P/E below its 15-year median with forward P/E under 15. Hover the pill for the reasons on that stock. 💧 Diluting — shares outstanding up 10% or more over 3 years; each share owns a shrinking slice of the company. ✂️ Buyback — shares outstanding down 10% or more over 3 years; buybacks shrank the share count, so each share owns a bigger slice. Score Score = buy score out of 10: Value, Health, Timing, Backing, Sentiment (2 points each). Tiers: 9–10 Strongest, 7–8 Solid, 4–6 Mixed, 0–3 Weak. RSI = 14-bar Wilder’s RSI on closed bars, shown under the Score; the arrow is the move vs the prior bar (↑ improving, ↓ worsening, → flat); above 70 is overbought. Sentiment = analyst consensus (Buy or better) + options flow (put/call volume below 1.0 = bullish). Columns Short = % of float sold short; days to cover underneath (days of average volume shorts need to exit) R40 = Rule of 40: revenue growth % + margin %; (EBITDA) uses EBITDA margin, (FCF) uses free cash flow margin. Bold green above 40%, red when negative, with the dominant leg’s % shown on the driver line. Margin trend = latest quarter’s EBITDA margin vs a year ago, in percentage points. Growth / Margin Driven — which leg contributes more than half of the Rule of 40 score: revenue growth or EBITDA margin. Insider = net $ of open-market insider trades, last 3 months (actual traded values from filings; awards and option exercises excluded) Insider $ highlighted green when net buying > $5M, red when net selling > $25M (last 3 months) 13F = major buys/sells by 15 famous active funds, Q3 2026 (filed Nov 2026). Major = new position, full exit (both ≥ $10M), or a change over $100M or 25% of the position. Funds: Buffett, Ackman, Tiger, Coatue, Lone Pine, Viking, Third Point, Tepper, Druckenmiller, Einhorn, Klarman, Soros, Elliott, D1, Cohen (Point72 is a multi-manager fund, so its moves reflect many independent pods). vs High = price vs highest price in the last 12 months (intraday, split-adjusted) Vol = last closed week’s volume vs its 20-week average; above 1.0× means heavier than usual; highlighted yellow at 2.0× or more Cash / Debt = total cash vs total debt; green cash = cash ≥ 2× debt, red debt = debt ≥ 2× cash (C = cash, D = debt) P/S & FCF: price/sales plus trailing-12-month free cash flow; YoY = latest quarter vs same quarter last year (quarterly FCF is lumpy — a near-zero quarter a year ago can make YoY very large) Avg P/E = median annual P/E over the last 10 / 15 fiscal years (actual year count in parentheses after each value). P/E (High) = the P/E at the stock’s 12-month high price, at current earnings Yellow P/E — earnings are too small or too distorted for the P/E to mean much; P/S shown bold amber on those rows — judge on P/S instead. P/E color — the P/E value wears a pill: green when cheap (25% or more below its own 15-year median and/or its sector median), red when expensive (25% or more above), plain when in between or the two disagree. Hover the P/E to see both comparisons. Earnings: latest quarter’s EPS surprise vs the analyst consensus — green at +5% or more, red at −5% or less, plain in between — with revenue growth year-over-year underneath. Revenue growth is green at +30% or more, red at −10% or less. The dots show the last three reported quarters, latest first. Cover: interest coverage — operating earnings ÷ interest expense. Green at 3× or more (healthy); amber from 1.5× to 3× (thin cover); red below 1.5× (interest not covered from earnings; negative means an operating loss). Banks and ETFs show no figure.

They are AAPL (Apple Inc.) (P/E 39.2, RSI 72.1), CRL (Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.) (P/E 356.4, RSI 72.7), HLT (Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc.) (P/E 48.9, RSI 74.5), KO (The Coca-Cola Company) (P/E 28.3, RSI 72.2), LLY (Eli Lilly and Company) (P/E 43.9, RSI 73.1) and MAR (Marriott International, Inc.) (P/E 41.3, RSI 70.8). The most stretched is CRL (Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.) — its P/E is +1,303% above its own 15y median, though at that level the P/E itself is distorted (see the yellow P/E note in How to read this); the cleanest cases are LLY (Eli Lilly and Company) and MAR (Marriott International, Inc.).

🔶 Near screaming sell on Monthly: 14 names — the flag does apply here, with the same definition as Weekly but on monthly RSI: overvalued with 14-month RSI 60–70, or overbought (14-month RSI > 70) with trailing P/E above its 15y median and forward P/E 15–20. Closest to the overbought line is DGX (Quest Diagnostics Incorporated), overvalued with monthly RSI 67.5; ABBV (AbbVie Inc.) and CAH (Cardinal Health, Inc.) qualify on the overbought leg. They carry the 🔶 flag in the monthly tables below, and the 🔶 filter below isolates them, just like on the Weekly tab.

Flags 🔺 Overvalued — trailing P/E above its own 15y median (10y fallback) & forward P/E above 20 🔶 Near screaming sell — applies on both tabs (Monthly uses 14-month RSI): overvalued with monthly RSI 60–70, or overbought with P/E above its median & fwd P/E 15–20 (14 names on the Nov intra-month list) Screaming sell — overvalued and overbought (see section above) 💎 Undervalued — trailing P/E < 12 & forward P/E < 15, no high-debt flag (a name can sit at the upper band and still be cheap on earnings) ⚠️ High debt — D/E > 2× or net debt > 50% of market cap 🔥 SQUEEZE = possible short squeeze setup: ≥10% of float short and ≥3 days to cover 📈 4H SMA ↑ / ➡️ 4H SMA → — 20-period SMA on 4-hour bars: ↑ rose more than 0.5% over the last 5 bars (~3 trading days), → flat within ±0.5%; no pill when it is falling 🪤 Potential trap: at least 3 of 5 warning signs — missed earnings last quarter; earnings expected to fall sharply (forward P/E over 1.5× trailing); negative cash flow or profitability; debt stress (interest cover under 1.5×, or high debt with cover under 2.5×); insiders or big funds selling heavily. Hover the pill for the reasons on that stock. 💸 Burning Cash — interest cover below 1.5× and cash runway under 2 years (cash ÷ annual cash burn). Earnings barely cover the interest bill and the cash pile runs out within two years at the current burn rate. 🎯 Potential opportunity: at least 4 of 5 positive signs — beat earnings in 2 of the last 3 quarters; net cash with comfortable interest cover; strong growth and cash generation (Rule of 40 over 40, positive cash flow); insiders or big funds buying; P/E below its 15-year median with forward P/E under 15. Hover the pill for the reasons on that stock. 💧 Diluting — shares outstanding up 10% or more over 3 years; each share owns a shrinking slice of the company. ✂️ Buyback — shares outstanding down 10% or more over 3 years; buybacks shrank the share count, so each share owns a bigger slice. Score Score = buy score out of 10: Value, Health, Timing, Backing, Sentiment (2 points each). Tiers: 9–10 Strongest, 7–8 Solid, 4–6 Mixed, 0–3 Weak. RSI = 14-bar Wilder’s RSI on closed bars, shown under the Score; the arrow is the move vs the prior bar (↑ improving, ↓ worsening, → flat); above 70 is overbought. Sentiment = analyst consensus (Buy or better) + options flow (put/call volume below 1.0 = bullish). Columns Short = % of float sold short; days to cover underneath (days of average volume shorts need to exit) R40 = Rule of 40: revenue growth % + margin %; (EBITDA) uses EBITDA margin, (FCF) uses free cash flow margin. Bold green above 40%, red when negative, with the dominant leg’s % shown on the driver line. Margin trend = latest quarter’s EBITDA margin vs a year ago, in percentage points. Growth / Margin Driven — which leg contributes more than half of the Rule of 40 score: revenue growth or EBITDA margin. Insider = net $ of open-market insider trades, last 3 months (actual traded values from filings; awards and option exercises excluded) Insider $ highlighted green when net buying > $5M, red when net selling > $25M (last 3 months) 13F = major buys/sells by 15 famous active funds, Q3 2026 (filed Nov 2026). Major = new position, full exit (both ≥ $10M), or a change over $100M or 25% of the position. Funds: Buffett, Ackman, Tiger, Coatue, Lone Pine, Viking, Third Point, Tepper, Druckenmiller, Einhorn, Klarman, Soros, Elliott, D1, Cohen (Point72 is a multi-manager fund, so its moves reflect many independent pods). vs High = price vs highest price in the last 12 months (intraday, split-adjusted) Vol = last closed month’s volume vs its 20-month average; above 1.0× means heavier than usual; highlighted yellow at 2.0× or more Cash / Debt = total cash vs total debt; green cash = cash ≥ 2× debt, red debt = debt ≥ 2× cash (C = cash, D = debt) P/S & FCF: price/sales plus trailing-12-month free cash flow; YoY = latest quarter vs same quarter last year (quarterly FCF is lumpy — a near-zero quarter a year ago can make YoY very large) Avg P/E = median annual P/E over the last 10 / 15 fiscal years (actual year count in parentheses after each value). P/E (High) = the P/E at the stock’s 12-month high price, at current earnings Yellow P/E — earnings are too small or too distorted for the P/E to mean much; P/S shown bold amber on those rows — judge on P/S instead. P/E color — the P/E value wears a pill: green when cheap (25% or more below its own 15-year median and/or its sector median), red when expensive (25% or more above), plain when in between or the two disagree. Hover the P/E to see both comparisons. Earnings: latest quarter’s EPS surprise vs the analyst consensus — green at +5% or more, red at −5% or less, plain in between — with revenue growth year-over-year underneath. Revenue growth is green at +30% or more, red at −10% or less. The dots show the last three reported quarters, latest first. Cover: interest coverage — operating earnings ÷ interest expense. Green at 3× or more (healthy); amber from 1.5× to 3× (thin cover); red below 1.5× (interest not covered from earnings; negative means an operating loss). Banks and ETFs show no figure.

About this snapshot: prices as of Thu 19 Nov 2026 close; band status vs the 20-week lower Bollinger Band (20-week, 2 std dev) from closed weeks. Short = % of float sold short, with days to cover underneath (days of average volume shorts need to exit). Insider figures are net dollars of open-market insider trades over the last 3 months (actual traded values from filings; awards and option exercises excluded) with open-market buy/sell transaction counts. Cash / Debt is total cash vs total debt, and the % under each price is vs the trailing-twelve-month high — the highest price in the last 12 months (intraday, split-adjusted). Monthly list: last updated 20 Nov 2026; developing intra-month read — band status vs the 20-month lower Bollinger Band (computed from closed months only) at latest November 2026 prices, fundamentals as of 20 Nov 2026; the confirmed list as of the Oct 2026 close was LII, XYL touching and BA, BKNG, T, TTWO, WY close; it is refreshed on the intra-month checks (10th, 20th and 28th) and on 1 Dec 2026 when November closes. This page is a fixed snapshot — it updates only when a new scan is published. 13F: major position changes by 15 tracked active funds in their Q3 2026 13F filings (period ended 30 Sep 2026, filed Nov 2026), sized at quarter-end prices; only the largest moves per stock are shown, sorted by net dollars. Avg P/E: median of annual year-end P/Es (fiscal year-end price ÷ diluted EPS from SEC filings, split-adjusted) over up to the last 10 and 15 fiscal years. Tops: the mirror scan — names at or near the 20-week / 20-month upper Bollinger Band, refreshed on the same schedule as the Bottoms lists; 🔺 overvalued means a trailing P/E above its own 15y median (10y fallback) with forward P/E above 20, and a screaming sell is overvalued and overbought (RSI > 70).
